findings.title: Security Disclosure: Wednesday October 21st
findings.summary_md: Railway's first public notice, published the morning of October 21, 2026, states that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted customer environment variables and, for some values, obtained the decrypted contents, including possible API keys and database credentials. The company told all users to revoke and reapply sensitive environment variables and paused every deployment while the investigation continued. At this stage Railway described the scope only as 'may have been accessed' and gave no workspace count, no attack timeline, and no dollar figure.

findings.title: Developer platform Railway urges 'all users' to revoke secret keys after cyberattack
findings.summary_md: TechCrunch reported on October 22, 2026 that Railway had confirmed a cyberattack allowed hackers to reach some customer secrets, prompting the company to urge all users to rotate credentials rather than only those notified individually. The piece is the first mainstream coverage of the disclosure and frames the incident as a platform-wide credential rotation event for a developer PaaS. It carries no exploitation detail beyond the unauthorized access Railway itself had confirmed.

findings.title: Preliminary Report: Oct 21st Security Incident
findings.summary_md: Railway's preliminary report, published October 22, 2026, fixes the intrusion window at October 20 13:58 UTC to October 22 03:32 UTC, roughly 26 hours. It repeats the instruction to revoke and reapply sensitive environment variables stored on Railway before that date and states that the investigation was still open. The report is the first Railway document to put times on the intrusion, which later reporting uses as the dwell-time baseline.

findings.title: Railway Platform Outage, resolved incident update QH8L8B3E
findings.summary_md: Railway's status page records that as of October 23, 2026 at 18:57:54 UTC it had finished notifying users whose workspaces met its criteria for increased risk, closing the notification phase of the incident. The same page tracks the deployment pause and restoration of builds rather than a separate incident. It gives no count of notified workspaces, leaving the affected population unquantified in Railway's own public record at that point.
